selection_rule: highest validation accuracy; earliest on ties
test_policy: single fixed-checkpoint evaluation; no optimizer, threshold search, epoch selection or retraining

published_reference.table: 8, Non-RD vs RD columns, UNet++ row

disclosures: Paper says AdamW; released experiment resolves to Adam. This first attempt follows pinned code, not a silently reconciled paper protocol.
One-GPU gradient accumulation and current dependency versions must be reported as hardware/software adaptations.
Independent PyTorch blocks replace MONAI wrappers; verify parameter and numerical parity against the read-only reference.
OpenCV decoding replaces torchvision/PyAV; grayscale/interpolation parity is checked, but cross-version decoder identity is not guaranteed.
Only float32 roundoff within 1e-6 is clipped at normalization boundaries.
Paper recall decimals do not reconcile with a simple 100-positive test denominator; exact reported-table agreement is not guaranteed.
Official splits are clip-level with possible same-patient overlap; no unseen-patient or clinical-validation claim.
FP16 autocast with FP32 master parameters and GradScaler replaces reference FP32, after a real-input finite-gradient timing probe. This numerical adaptation is not bit-identical training.
Kaggle platform: two saved CPU-preparation outputs preserve all float32 inputs; GPU jobs attach them read-only.
Only CUDA device 0 is used, including on a T4 x2 allocation; this is not distributed training.
Training proceeds in saved bounded notebook jobs; completed prior output must be attached to continue.
